messages:
infra-deploy-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 decode tail latency spike + streaming stalls observed across us-west-2. Auto-pager triggered. Affected model: redwood-7B-v2 (hosted).

maya (eng-oncall): acked. I'm on it. First pass: correlate with recent infra changes — rolled TRT8 kernels + new compile flags landed last night.

maya (eng-oncall): quick customer impact check: customer-support any reports of disconnects or visible errors?

customer-support: got 4 threads flagged by customers using streaming endpoints (live chat, doc-summarize). Symptoms: streams stall mid-response, client sees long stall then reconnect. No data loss reported but UX broken.

sophie (eng-sre): metrics: p95 steady, p99 jumped ~5x for decode tail (60ms -> 320ms) since 03:10 UTC. Memory paging correlated on some nodes; kernel context shows increased page faults around the same time.

raj (eng-runtime): rolling log snippet from a degraded host:```
[decode] kernel=trt8-2026.03.11 build=opt-batch-v2
stream_id=xx pid=4521 tail-latency=312ms page-faults=112
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.78
```
Notable: we enabled `TRT_BATCH_MERGE=1` + `FLASHATTN_ALGO=auto` in compile flags last night. Suspect new kernel path choosing a FlashAttention variant that triggers worst-case memory access patterns for longer seqs.

maya (eng-oncall): hypothesis: new TRT8 kernels + auto flashattn + aggressive batching merged requests -> larger memory working set -> paging -> tail latency spikes/stalls. Mitigation options: 1) pin runtime to trt7-compat on affected pool, 2) disable TRT_BATCH_MERGE or FLASHATTN_ALGO=auto, 3) route streaming traffic to fallback lighter model, 4) enable more aggressive KV-prefix caching to reduce decode work.

sophie (eng-sre): immediate live mitigations I'd run in order: 
- pin kernel on 6 affected hosts to `trt7-compat-2026.02` (fast rollback)
- toggle compile flag `FLASHATTN_ALGO=deterministic` in canary pools
- update router policy to divert 20% of streaming requests to fallback variant `redwood-7B-quant` (lower mem)
- raise eviction threshold for KV cache to 75%

raj (eng-runtime): commands to pin kernel (run on infra orchestrator):```

infractl kernel pin --hosts host-az1-{12..17} --kernel trt7-compat-2026.02 --reason "hotfix: decode tail latency"
# watch logs: infractl host tail host-az1-12 /var/log/decode.log | grep tail-latency
```
I'll prepare a rollback patch for the compile flags but that's slower (recompile + deploy).

maya (eng-oncall): go for pin + router diversion. Sophie, can you coordinate router change? Raj, start pin. I'll update customers and set severity.

ops-bot: Severity set to Sev2 by maya (eng-oncall). Pager escalation: ops-oncall -> eng-runtime -> eng-sre.

customer-support: sending initial customer message: "We're investigating higher-than-normal streaming latency affecting some responses; engineering is triaging and a mitigation is rolling out. We'll follow up within 30m."

(10m later)
raj (eng-runtime): pinned kernels on targets. Early telemetry: p99 dropped from 320ms -> 150ms on pinned hosts. Paging counts down ~70%.

sophie (eng-sre): router change applied: 25% traffic diverted to fallback quantized variant. Observed immediate drop in overall error/retry rate on the cluster.

maya (eng-oncall): good. Customer impact summary so far: about 6 customers saw degraded streaming; for three customers p99 > 250ms causing degraded UX. No SLO breaches for p95. We're in mitigation stage, not full rollback.

evan (product): which contracts are at risk? Any Dedicated customers with SLAs impacted? Need list for escalation to account teams.

customer-support: two Dedicated tenants (acme-inc, healthflow) reported incidents; acme has 99.9% latency SLA per monthly commit. We'll flag both for account team outreach.

raj (eng-runtime): root-cause hypothesis refined: `FLASHATTN_ALGO=auto` picks a tiled algorithm for longer sequences that uses larger scratch allocations. Combined with `TRT_BATCH_MERGE=1`, we create larger fused batches that exceed per-GPU working set causing OS-level page-in spikes. On older trt7 variant the kernel path used a streaming-friendly algo and didn't allocate as much.

maya (eng-oncall): action items for immediate post-incident: 
- Keep pinned kernel until we ship a validated trt8 build with deterministic flashattn algo (owner: raj)
- Revert `TRT_BATCH_MERGE` feature toggle to default-off for streaming routes (owner: maya)
- Add regression test to CI that runs long-seq streaming workload for tail-latency checks (owner: eng-ml)
- Notify account team + customers with ETA for next update (owner: customer-support)

sophie (eng-sre): monitoring follow-up: add alert for page-fault spikes correlated with tail-latency > 200ms (owner: eng-sre). Also add a synthetic streaming probe at 512 token seqs to Canary to catch this.

raj (eng-runtime): plan for safe TRT8 re-onboard: build trt8 with `FLASHATTN_ALGO=deterministic`, test with merged-batch sizes up to 128, run overnight regression harness across canary hosts. After validation, enable `TRT_BATCH_MERGE` behind a canary flag and ramp slowly.

maya (eng-oncall): handoff: I'm heading offline for next 40m. Handoff to raj (eng-runtime). Summary for raj: incident started ~03:10 UTC after TRT8 + compile flags rollout, mitigation pinned trt7-compat on affected hosts and diverted traffic; p99 improved but keep monitoring p99/p95, page faults, and streaming stalls. Priority: complete safe re-onboard plan and CI regression.

raj (eng-runtime): taking over. I'll coordinate the rollback flag and run the canary plan. If anything regresses, I'll escalate back to Sev1.

infra-deploy-bot: note: kernel pin completed; change-id: ch-98765; requested by raj.

sophie (eng-sre): post-mortem checklist added to incident: include timeline, root-cause analysis, mitigations, follow-ups, and owners. Target postmortem publish within 72h.

maya (eng-oncall): thanks all. closing on-call note: current state = mitigated, monitoring. We will keep the pin for 24-48h pending regression tests.

raj (eng-runtime): quick debug note for postmortem: include sampling of `strace` of a stalled decode process to show page-fault stack, and kernel diffs between trt7/trt8 that affect allocator behavior.

customer-support: I'll follow up with customers with status update and expected timeline for full resolution.

(End of thread)
